source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / Directorate General of Agriculture, "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកសៀង" [Soybean cultivation techniques], official extension manual, 2018
text: The manual defines three post-planting monitoring windows for farmers to check the crop: Stage 1 — germination and root establishment, checking that soil moisture is adequate and cotyledons/first leaves emerge cleanly; Stage 2 — first true leaves and early nodulation, checking that plants are not stressed and roots are developing well; Stage 3 — root and nodule development continuing, checking specifically for visible root nodules (the sign that Rhizobium infection has succeeded) since this determines the crop's own nitrogen self-sufficiency going forward. Specific percentage/day figures printed in this section of the source were not fully legible and are omitted here rather than guessed, per project convention.
